scores.claim_text: Teal Drones (RCAT subsidiary) was selected in November 2024 as a winner of the U.S. Army's Short Range Reconnaissance (SRR) Program of Record; Black Widow is the SRR product accepted into the Army program.
supports: pentagon_jbook returned NOT_FOUND for 'Short Range Reconnaissance' (program_name), 'SRR' (program_name), 'Teal Drones' (contractor) and 'Red Cat' (contractor). The J-Book corpus is restricted to Air Force RDT&E (269), Defense-wide incl. DARPA/MDA/SOCOM/OSD (74), and Space Force (67) — NO Army programs are present in the 410-PE corpus (Counter check confirmed 0 Army entries). SRR is an Army Program of Record so coverage gap applies (per Heuristic 7, NOT_FOUND outside corpus scope → UNVERIFIABLE).

USAspending shows TEAL DRONES INC with 27 DoD awards totaling only $2.16M lifetime; NONE are labeled SRR / Black Widow / Short Range Reconnaissance. Largest awards are individual Teal 2 buys ($750K USAFA, $240K VA National Guard) — not a Program-of-Record production lot. This is consistent with Army SRR Lot 1 production contracts being either (a) not yet obligated on USAspending at cutoff or (b) bundled under a parent prime not visible here. The claim of SRR PoR selection is not directly disprovable from these sources.
scores.M_value: NOT_FOUND (Army programs outside J-Book corpus scope)
scores.interpretation: Coverage gap, not a red flag. The Signal OS J-Book corpus does not include Army RDT&E or Army Procurement P-40 lines, so it cannot verify the SRR Program of Record either way. USAspending shows minimal Teal Drones obligations and zero labeled SRR awards as of cutoff — note this as a coverage limitation rather than a divergence finding.

scores.claim_text: FY 2025 consolidated revenue of $40.7M (up 128% vs FY 2024 $17.8M; up 739% vs eight-month Transition Period $4.9M) is attributable primarily to the commencement and scaling of drone deliveries to the U.S. Army under the SRR program.
supports: Company attributes $40.7M FY2025 revenue primarily to SRR deliveries to the U.S. Army.

USAspending shows TEAL DRONES INC with $2.16M TOTAL DoD obligations across 27 awards (lifetime, all entities). Even allowing for FY25 timing, the recipient-name dataset shows no awards remotely matching the order-of-magnitude required to support $40.7M in SRR-attributed FY25 revenue. The largest single Teal Drones obligation in the dataset is $750K (USAFA, 74 Teal 2 drones).

Per Heuristic 6 (USAspending cross-check): if the company claims revenue from a named program and USAspending shows orders of magnitude less, the original revenue attribution may be inflated OR the contracts are obligated under a prime contractor / OTA / non-standard vehicle invisible to recipient_name queries.
pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for SRR (Army not in corpus) — cannot independently verify forward-year SRR funding trajectory.
scores.M_value: USAspending: $2.16M lifetime / 27 awards / 0 SRR-labeled. pentagon_jbook: NOT_FOUND (corpus gap).
scores.interpretation: Material under-delivery signal in the orthogonal source. The 20x gap between claimed $40.7M FY25 SRR revenue and observable $2.16M lifetime USAspending obligations to TEAL DRONES INC is a verifier divergence worth flagging. Caveats: (i) SRR Lot 1 obligations may be too recent to appear; (ii) Army production contracts on PoR can flow through OTA vehicles or prime contractors and not show under the sub's recipient name; (iii) J-Book Army coverage gap prevents forward-year confirmation. Severity SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY rather than RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE because the USAspending lag/routing caveats are real and the company is publicly named as an SRR selectee — the framework should flag but not call fraud. If the parent agent observes that this is the load-bearing thesis claim (FY26 forward narrative hinges entirely on SRR scaling), promote to RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE.

scores.claim_text: Black Widow flight tested with Palantir VNav software, marketed as the first commercial demo of visual navigation software on a drone 'already accepted into a U.S. Army program' (forward narrative of Army program-of-record continuity).
supports: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND — Army SRR is outside the 410-PE J-Book corpus.

Claim is a forward narrative / technology-integration milestone, not a current revenue commitment. The 'already accepted' language is consistent with the Nov-2024 SRR selection (Claim C1) and inherits its verifier status.
scores.interpretation: Inherits UNVERIFIABLE from C1. Coverage-gap finding.

scores.claim_text: FANG FPV drones are being developed as a payload deployable from AeroVironment's P550 UAS under a marsupial configuration, leveraging MOSA architecture (forward pipeline tied to AV's P550, which is itself an Army Future Tactical UAS / FTUAS-adjacent platform).
supports: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for 'Future Tactical Unmanned Aircraft System', 'FTUAS', and 'AeroVironment' (contractor) — both Army RDT&E PEs and AV's procurement lines are outside the present J-Book corpus.
Claim is a development roadmap (no booked revenue) — even with full coverage, this would be jbook_program_pipeline (forward), not jbook_program_revenue.
scores.interpretation: Coverage gap. Cannot test FTUAS funding trajectory or AV's procurement exposure with current corpus.

scores.claim_text: Teal 2 is Blue UAS Certified by the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD list of approved sUAS for government use).
supports: USAspending corroborates real (if small) DoD purchasing of Teal 2 systems across multiple commands (USAFA, VA National Guard, Patrick SFB, etc.) — consistent with Blue UAS list eligibility.
Claim is binary (certified yes/no), not a forward-revenue claim — low underdelivery exposure.
scores.M_value: 27 awards, $2.16M; multiple Teal 2 buys including 'BLUE UAS CERTIFIED LIST' explicit in W912LQ25FA019 description
scores.interpretation: Verified — Blue UAS certification supported by award descriptions explicitly referencing the Blue UAS Cleared List.

scores.claim_text: Blue Ops, Inc. division (launched August 2025) is developing a family of USV (uncrewed surface vessel) weapons systems for defense markets — forward pipeline narrative tied to Navy/DoD USV demand.
supports: pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding(program_name='Maritime Systems') returned SOCOM PE 1160483BB with status FUNDED_SHRINKING: FY24 $158.9M → FY25 $200.8M → FY26 $120.5M (40% YoY cut in FY26).
SOCOM Unmanned ISR (PE 1160434BB) returned FUNDED_SHRINKING: FY24 $6.7M → FY25 $31.6M → FY26 $2.3M (93% YoY cut in FY26).
Per Heuristic 1, FUNDED_SHRINKING → MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY for claimed-program-revenue claims. Blue Ops is a forward pipeline (no booked revenue yet) so materiality (Heuristic 2) is limited.
scores.M_value: Maritime Systems FUNDED_SHRINKING (FY26 $120M, -40% YoY); Unmanned ISR FUNDED_SHRINKING (FY26 $2.3M, -93% YoY)
scores.interpretation: Closest J-Book proxies for the USV/maritime-unmanned demand the Blue Ops thesis relies on are both shrinking in the FY26 PB. The Blue Ops launch narrative collides with a contracting SOCOM USV/unmanned ISR funding envelope. Note: this is a SOCOM proxy, not a direct Navy USV PE.

scores.claim_text: Going-concern context: company has accumulated deficit of $196.8M at Dec 31, 2025 and has 'never been profitable'; ability to generate higher revenues and profitability depends on continued execution of Army programs.
supports: Self-disclosed in 10-K — no external verifier needed for the disclosure itself.

Relevant as financial backdrop for scoring SRR-dependence claims (C2 above): with $196.8M accumulated deficit and never-profitable history, the company's solvency thesis is load-bearingly dependent on SRR scaling. This amplifies the materiality weight of any C2 underdelivery.
scores.interpretation: Disclosed accurately; included as context that elevates materiality of the SRR-revenue dependence flagged in C2.
